source: Biology Textbook pp. 193-239 (PDF primary) + Mermaid mindmap

bullets: Xavier Bichat (1771–1802) coined the term 'tissue'; he is both Father and Founder of animal histology; distinguished 21 types of elementary tissues — without a microscope.
Karl Mayer (1801) coined the term 'histology'; Marcello Malpighi (1628–1694) is the Founder of histology.
Phylum Coelenterata is the first phylum to possess animal tissue (tissue grade of organization).
Animal tissues are classified into four types based on origin, structure, location, and function: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, and Nervous tissue.
Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces, lines cavities, forms glands, and secretes enzymes/hormones.
It is avascular (no blood vessels) — nutrition and gas exchange occur by diffusion through the basement membrane (made of white collagen).
Epithelium has minimal matrix; all cells are held together by four cell junctions: Tight junction, Adherens junction, Desmosome (Macula adherens), and Gap junction.
Surfaces by coelom type: Acoelomate (flatworm) = 2 surfaces; Pseudocoelomate (roundworm) = 3 surfaces; Coelomate (earthworm) = 4 surfaces.
Originated from all three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.
Two major classifications by layers: Simple epithelium (single layer) and Compound epithelium (multiple layers).

bullets: Connective tissue is the most abundant animal tissue; it binds, supports, and circulates.
Originated from mesoderm; has fewer cells, most abundant matrix, and abundant fibres.
Three main types: Proper CT (binds), Supportive CT (Cartilage + Bone — supports), Fluid CT (Blood + Lymph — circulates).
Proper CT fibres: Collagen/White fibres (inelastic, in bundles); Elastic/Yellow fibres (branched, elastic); Reticulate/Colourless fibres (form stroma framework).
Cartilage is avascular; Bone is vascular — both are supportive CT.
Blood = 55% Plasma + 45% Blood cells (RBCs, WBCs, Platelets).

bullets: Muscular tissue (muscle) is contractile tissue; mesodermal in origin.

Three types: Skeletal/Striped/Striated (voluntary — fatigues immediately); Smooth/Unstriped/Non-striated (involuntary — fatigues after ~10–12 hrs); Cardiac/Heart muscle (involuntary — never fatigues).
Cardiac muscle has intercalated discs separating individual cardiocytes.
Red muscle has myoglobin (e.g., man, goat); White muscle lacks myoglobin (e.g., athletes, fish).
sections.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[Muscular Tissue] --> B[Skeletal / Voluntary]
  A --> C[Smooth / Involuntary]
  A --> D[Cardiac / Involuntary]

bullets: Nervous tissue controls, coordinates, integrates, and regulates organisms; ectodermal in origin.
Two cell types: Neuroglia (supportive non-neuronal cells — can do mitosis) and Neurones (structural + functional unit — cannot do mitosis).
Neurone parts: Soma (Cyton/cell body — gray) + Neurites (Dendrite — afferent/sensory; Axon — efferent/motor).
Myelinated neurones are white (fast conduction, Nodes of Ranvier); Non-myelinated neurones are gray (slow conduction).
Gray matter = outer brain + inner spinal cord; White matter = inner brain + outer spinal cord.
